answer: A mountain valley stays honest when every new identity must carry a distinct sealed letter on foot over a different high pass, stamped by a distinct pass-keeper, and each next identity crosses twice as many passes. The first fake crosses one pass, the second two, the third four, doubling each time, so the tenth fake alone owes 512 crossings and twenty fakes would owe over a million. Bulk farming fails because a gale on the ridge halts every caravan at once, a whisper of forgery sends a ripple through the valley ledgers, and one courier cannot walk a million passes before snow closes them.
